title: Modi Meets Tokayev, El-Sisi as Xi and Putin Depart After BRICS Summit
excerpt: On the final day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the prime minister held bilateral talks with Kazakhstan's Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, as the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration and Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin departed.
body:
• The 18th BRICS Summit concluded Sunday in New Delhi, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi holding bilateral talks with Kazakhstan's Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's Abdel Fattah El-Sisi on the final day.
  • The Modi-El-Sisi meeting reviewed the India-Egypt Strategic Partnership, with El-Sisi pitching manufacturing, clean energy and the Suez Canal Economic Zone, and Modi urging Indian companies to invest in Egypt.
  • The Modi-Tokayev meeting reaffirmed the India-Kazakhstan strategic partnership across trade, defence, energy, critical minerals and emerging technologies.
  • The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration, with consensus on West Asia through dialogue and diplomacy; Xi and Putin departed after the event, and China takes over the rotating BRICS chair.

The two-day 18th BRICS Summit wrapped up Sunday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi capping a marathon of summit diplomacy with bilateral meetings with Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi. Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin departed India as the summit concluded, closing a gathering that tested the expanded bloc's ability to speak with one voice.

The Egypt meeting: a push for economic substance

Modi met El-Sisi on Sunday, with the two leaders reviewing the India-Egypt Strategic Partnership across trade, defence, technology and clean energy. According to Egyptian presidency spokesperson Mohamed El-Shenawy, El-Sisi underlined the urgency of concrete steps to deepen the partnership, focusing on manufacturing, technology, clean energy and the automotive sector.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2099081076195131846

El-Sisi pointed to Egypt's advantages for Indian firms — its location, workforce, free-trade-agreement network and incentives under the Suez Canal Economic Zone. Modi encouraged Indian companies to scale up investments in Egypt and deepen business-community linkages.

Egypt has been a full BRICS member since January 2024. El-Sisi had also met Putin on the sidelines on Saturday; according to Russia's foreign ministry, Putin invited him to Moscow in October for the Russia-Africa Summit.

The Kazakhstan meeting: strategic partnership reaffirmed

Modi's meeting with Tokayev reviewed cooperation across political ties, trade, defence and security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals, emerging technologies, the creative economy and people-to-people exchanges, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs. Modi recalled India's ancient civilisational ties with Kazakhstan and expressed satisfaction at the steady growth of bilateral relations. The leaders, the MEA said, "reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries, for the mutual benefit of their people, as well as for peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region." NSA Ajit Doval, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and MEA Secretary (West) Sibi George attended the talks.

Modi-Xi: a commitment on the border

The most closely watched bilateral came Saturday evening, when Modi met Xi — the Chinese leader's first trip to India since the 2019 Mamallapuram summit and the first since the 2020 Galwan clash. India's foreign ministry said afterward that the two leaders had agreed to work together toward resolving their contested border.

"Although our two countries are different in many respects, they are fully capable of complementing each other's strengths, supporting one another, achieving mutual success and advancing together."

— Xi Jinping, in remarks at his meeting with PM Modi

The meeting followed the 25th round of Special Representative talks in Beijing on August 28 between NSA Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.

A summit of tests for the expanded bloc

India hosted the summit under its fourth BRICS chairmanship — after 2012, 2016 and 2021 — on the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." The enlarged grouping now counts 11 full members, including Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia, alongside 10 partner countries including Kazakhstan, Malaysia and Vietnam. Modi led India's effort to drive consensus among members with competing geopolitical interests.

The summit produced the New Delhi Declaration. According to MEA Secretary (Economic Relations) Sudhakar Dalela, BRICS reached consensus on West Asia, with dialogue and diplomacy as the guiding principles for addressing conflicts — a formulation bridging divides including the Iran-UAE split deepened by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Leaders also visited the Bharat Innovates exposition, showcasing 37 Indian deep-tech innovations.

The gathering underscored India's balancing act: Russia remains one of its largest energy suppliers even as New Delhi faces pressure from Washington over Russian oil purchases.

The view from the diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the summit's significance lies less in ceremony than in economics: India's turn chairing an expanded BRICS put New Delhi's decisions on trade, energy security and cross-border payments at the centre of the Global South's agenda — choices that ripple through the global markets in which diaspora savings and investments sit.

What's next

China takes over the rotating BRICS chair following the New Delhi summit. The tests ahead: whether the West Asia consensus and the Modi-Xi border commitment produce follow-through, and how the bloc's parallel relationships play out — starting with El-Sisi's October trip to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit.
